definition: The electrical work a source, such as a cell, does on each unit of charge to move it round a complete circuit; it is measured in volts (V); Extended students also use $E = \frac{W}{Q}$.
The work done by each unit of charge as it passes through a component, which is the energy it transfers there; it is measured in volts (V); Extended students also use $V = \frac{W}{Q}$.
A meter that measures potential difference (or e.m.f.) in volts; it is connected in parallel, across the component, and has a very high resistance so that almost no current passes through it.
